metadata.title: SpaceX stock declines post-earnings. Are investors worried about AI spending?

content.text:
SpaceX stock (SPCX) is losing altitude and shedding yesterday's stock gains over the AI spending forecasts reported in its first-ever earnings release.
Morning Brief Host Julie Hyman is joined by Yahoo Finance Senior Reporter Pras Subramanian and Breaking News Reporter Jake Conley to break down SpaceX's negative stock moves.
SpaceX coming out with its first earnings report as a public company. Revenue up by 92%. It is spending more, about $18.4 billion in the second quarter, raises forecast for that spending for the full year. The stock has been trading lower this morning. It's been trending lower since pretty much since the IPO after a little pop after the IPO. It also announced a big partnership with Nvidia. Um, so give it like what stood out to you now that you've had a little time to sleep hopefully and like digest all of all of the all of what you heard.
So it's a long application period. I mean there was a I mean there's a lot to cover here. Uh I guess first and foremost, I think you remember yesterday the stock was up a decent amount before the report.
Uh people can, you know, thinking about maybe this is short covering ahead of this and then had the earnings report which was the numbers Jake and I were talking about, the numbers coming out looked very positive. Like good beats here. Uh the businesses, various businesses are doing well.
Now you had that CAPEX, AI CAPEX number that was bigger than expected and I think people are are a little bit uh concerned about that.
I've seen a couple of notes that have said it has to do with the pending unlock of the ability to sell shares, which happens tomorrow. Right, exactly. So that that that perhaps is more of the pressure on the shares still because, you know, you have that lock up and then you have a bunch of other ones um expiring before the end of the year.
Yeah, and I think that makes sense. I I just I just have to wonder, we knew this was coming up, so you think that that already be priced in in some respect, right?
You would think that people would get ahead of it. But there's going to be a huge, potentially huge amount of shares coming online tomorrow. Uh so that's you're right, that's that's a concern. And it's the question is how much of that, how many people will actually sell?
That's right. It's not as though everyone is going to unload their shares.
That's right. Revenue looked good. EPS looked better than expected, EBITDA looked better than expected. It was that AI CAPEX number, which was about double what the street was looking for that really sent that stock falling, sent some of those worries.
Is it worth it when you're already a rocketry company, when you're already a satellite company, when you're already doing all these other really expensive, really hard businesses to try to also be one of the world's leading hyperscalers and to spend all of that money.
And what's the CAPEX figure for the full year that they're looking for?
Um because for the second quarter, it was in line or a little bit lower even than than what was expected.
It's the CAPEX number for the full year.
So they they didn't they didn't give a projection, but JP Morgan uh says that 2027 capacity will be 200 billion and in 2028. uh and that and that's of course not just not just, you know, the space business, it's it's that's like you mentioned the AI business.
It's mostly the AI business.
